text:
devin: follow-up thread from RFC: alternative reconciliation for per-tenant decaying-credit. want design checks before i update the doc.
anya: quick recap? we moved off fixed-window counters to exp-decay credits at admission, right?
kevin: yes. main problem area is cross-router convergence when routers hold divergent credit snapshots. we need a low-cost merge and fast repair plan.
rachel: idea: keep each router's credit as (value, last_ts, router_id). on merge we compute decayed values to a common epoch, then pick max(value) and set last_ts = max(last_ts). avoids double-counting.
devin: picking max may starve legitimate distributed usage if routers are slightly behind and both granted some units. how do we prevent lost grants?
kevin: agree. propose split-merge: routers keep delta-logs of grants since last-sync. merge = decayed_base + sum(deltas) where deltas are idempotent and bounded. still small metadata.
anya: delta-log size might blow up for noisy tenants. limit with per-router aggregation windows and compaction. we only need accurate totals at 1s granularity for admission workloads.
rachel: SLA-wise, worst-case drift should be bounded to <1% of tenant quota per minute. is that acceptable?
devin: targets: p99 latency unchanged, and quota drift < 2% per 5m. if we can meet that we can roll.
kevin: storage question: where to keep persisted credit blobs? local router memory + periodic checkpoint to central KV (etcd/consul). on restart router reloads checkpoint and applies local delta log.
anya: also need an escape hatch: force-sync endpoint on admission that can take authoritative snapshot for a tenant and push to routers. for operator debugging too.
rachel: operator UX: a CLI to sample tenant's distributed credits and compute a reconciliation diff. ops-bot: will add a ticket template.
devin: API sketch for admission <-> router, v1: {
  "tenant": "t123",
  "request_units": 5,
  "router_id": "r-az1-12"
} -> response:
{
  "granted": 5,
  "remaining_credit": 824.5,
  "last_updated_ts": 1745139876,
  "decay_half_life_ms": 180000
}
kevin: add a "snapshot_epoch" field so routers can detect stale responses. also a small signing HMAC for tamper detection.
anya: about telemetry: we need per-tenant credit divergence metric: sample credits from two independent routers for same tenant and record relative difference. set alert if >5% for >2mins.
devin: rollout plan idea: - implement merge-and-compaction in simulator - run against 60-day replay with spike scenarios - feature-flag admission responses (shadow mode) - 2w shadow real traffic on 5% of routers - enable for low-rate tenants first, then scale. revert criteria: p95 latency +5% or unexpected throttles >0.3%.
rachel: add canary metric: "throttle-unexpected" where clients that historically never saw throttles suddenly do. wire to pager if rate high.
kevin: question: do we let routers locally grant ahead using local soft-credit to reduce latency? risk is oversubscribe. maybe allow only for tier-B tenants with small budgets.
anya: i like soft-credit but with strict reconciliation windows and capped horizon. e.g., allow local speculative grant up to 10% of tenant budget for max 200ms.
devin: we should document safety properties: atomicity: admission grants are idempotent, reconciliation is monotonic, repair uses authoritative checkpoint if divergence > threshold.
rachel: ops needs a runbook: how to trigger authoritative reset, how to detect split-brain, how to fast-forward checkpoints. ops-bot: creating runbook stub INFRA-8201.
kevin: simulator items: measure false-throttle rate, latency delta, and reconciliation traffic overhead. i can add a smoke job.
anya: i'll add synthetic client patterns: sustained, bursty, long-tail sessions.
devin: ok. final asks: @kevin implement prototype merge logic, @anya add simulator scenarios, @rachel produce runbook draft, @devin update RFC with new merge/compaction section. ops-bot: created tracker INFRA-8201 (https://tracker/redwood/INFRA-8201).
ops-bot: note: will auto-create alert templates for credit-divergence and unexpected-throttle.
